analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. docs/provider/cli-reference.md bumps the date to 2026-10-22 (line 3) and adds two benchmark flags to the `darkbloom benchmark` table: `--runtime-concurrency` and `--runtime-stagger` (head lines 1208-1209, plus the runtime-generation row near line 564). docs/reference/configuration.md adds two env-var rows, `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED` and `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY` (head lines 401-402).

No code, auth, attestation, encryption or coordinator wire behavior changes. The documented flags are benchmark-only diagnostics. They run through the production CBv2 slot with prefix cache off, so they do not touch the T-041 SSD cache gate, TTL, name derivation or scope. They add no new network surface, and the benchmark JSON carries model/prompt/token hashes rather than consumer data.

The new env knobs tune Qwen MTP decode/carry behavior. The docs state they are not forwarded to LaunchAgents, which limits them to foreground/local operator control. This is consistent with the existing trust model: the operator is an adversary only for attestation and weights (T-012, T-013), not for their own throughput tuning. I could not verify that the referenced MTPContractsV2.swift defaults or the non-forwarding claim match the code, because those sources were not supplied. Even so, MTP decode path changes would affect correctness, not confidentiality, and the documentation text creates no security regression. The cli-reference.md passthrough table (lines 1735-1754) is unchanged, which is consistent with the claim that these variables are not forwarded.

No threat-model update is needed from these doc changes. Remaining question: the underlying code change in libs/mlx-swift-lm (not in this batch) should be reviewed separately for MTP correctness and memory behavior.
